lines.en: The year is 100 CE, and 11-year-old Julia Lucilla is playing with her ivory doll Pompeia.
lines.zh: 时值公元一〇〇年，十一岁的朱莉娅·露西拉正在玩她的象牙娃娃庞培娅。

lines.en: Named after the Roman Emperor Trajan’s wife, Pompeia is only 20 centimeters tall, with joints at her arms, legs, knees, and elbows, and a bevy of miniature clothes and accessories.
lines.zh: 庞培娅的名字取自罗马皇帝图拉真的妻子，身高只有二十厘米，手臂、腿、膝盖和肘部都有关节，还配了一大堆迷你衣服和配饰。

lines.en: With her doll in hand, Julia hosts elaborate dinner parties, helps Aeneas escape Troy, and accompanies her father on work trips to Egypt.
lines.zh: 带着这个娃娃，朱莉娅会举办精致的晚宴，帮助埃涅阿斯逃出特洛伊，也会陪父亲去埃及出差。

lines.en: This ancient scene is likely familiar to any modern parent, and that’s because kids have been going on imaginary adventures with their toys for thousands of years.
lines.zh: 这幅古代的场景，今天的父母多半会觉得眼熟——因为几千年来，孩子们一直带着玩具去进行想象中的冒险。

lines.en: While the most common ancient playthings would likely have been sticks and rocks, evidence of their use for play is archaeologically invisible.
lines.zh: 古代最常见的玩具很可能是树枝和石头，但它们被用来玩耍这件事，在考古上是看不出来的。

lines.en: However, archaeologists have found material, visual, and written evidence for toys across the ancient world.
lines.zh: 不过，考古学家还是在世界各地找到了有关玩具的实物、图像和文字证据。

lines.en: In Anatolia circa 3000 BCE, miniature toy carriages raced through the dirt at the hands of energetic youngsters.
lines.zh: 大约在公元前三千年，安纳托利亚的迷你玩具车在精力充沛的孩子手里，飞驰过泥土路面。

lines.en: A thousand years later, in the Indus Valley, a toddler giggled gleefully at the chirping sound created by their dove-shaped terracotta whistle.
lines.zh: 一千年后，在印度河流域，一个刚学会走路的小孩被手中鸽子形状的陶哨发出的啾啾声逗得咯咯直笑。

lines.en: Alongside whistles and wheeled toys, dolls are another common ancient plaything, though they can be a little harder to identify.
lines.zh: 除了哨子和带轮子的玩具，娃娃也是古代常见的玩具之一，只是它们有时不太容易辨认。

lines.en: While some archaeologists think ancient female figurines found across Afro-Eurasia may have been children’s toys, others believe them to be sacred fertility idols.
lines.zh: 有些考古学家认为，在非洲至欧亚大陆各地发现的古代女性小雕像可能是儿童的玩具；另一些人则认为，它们是用于祈求生育的神圣偶像。

lines.en: But we do know dolls like Pompeia were popular in Greece and Rome, with hair and clothes designed to reflect changing adult fashions.
lines.zh: 不过可以确定的是，像庞培娅这样的娃娃在希腊和罗马相当流行，它们的发型和衣着会跟着成人时尚的变化而改变。

lines.en: And thousands of years later in the Arctic, Inuit children carried fur-clad dolls carved of wood or walrus tusk.
lines.zh: 几千年后，在北极地区，因纽特的孩子会带着用木头或海象牙刻成、身上裹着毛皮的娃娃。

lines.en: But perhaps the most common ancient toy is the humble ball.
lines.zh: 但古代最常见的玩具，也许要数那不起眼的球。

lines.en: Thousands of years ago, children in ancient Egypt, China, Greece, and Mesoamerica kicked and threw balls made of everything from leather and linen to papyrus and palm fiber.
lines.zh: 几千年前，古埃及、中国、希腊和中美洲的孩子们踢着、扔着各种各样材质的球——从皮革、亚麻，到莎草纸和棕榈纤维，什么都能拿来做一个。

lines.en: The rules for most of their games have been lost to time, however some kids may have imitated adult games we know more about.
lines.zh: 这些游戏的规则大多已经随时间失传，不过有些孩子可能是在模仿我们了解较多的成人游戏。

lines.en: For example, ancient Greek children might have played episkuros, a team sport where players competed to push their opponents outside the pitch by hurling the ball as far as possible.
lines.zh: 比如说，古希腊的孩子可能玩过一种叫 episkuros 的球类游戏：这是一种团队运动，双方比着把球扔得更远，把对手逼出场地。

lines.en: Meanwhile, Mesoamerican kids might have played a game where players try to hit a rubber ball through a hoop using only their hips.
lines.zh: 与此同时，中美洲的孩子可能玩过这样一种游戏：只能靠髋部的动作，把橡胶球打过一个石环。

lines.en: Then again, in some cultures, this game had religious significance, so it's possible those children steered clear of this sacred sport.
lines.zh: 不过话说回来，在有些文化里，这种游戏带有宗教意义，所以那些孩子也许反而会避开这项神圣的运动。

lines.en: In any case, rougher, physical play was often limited by ancient gender expectations, with young girls being left out of rowdier ball games in Rome and Egypt.
lines.zh: 无论如何，那些更激烈、更带身体对抗的玩耍，往往会受到古代性别观念的限制——在罗马和埃及，小女孩就被排除在比较粗野的球类游戏之外。

lines.en: Spartan girls circa 400 BCE did engage in the same rigorous physical activities as boys, but largely because adults believed it would strengthen their bodies for childbearing.
lines.zh: 大约公元前四百年，斯巴达的女孩确实和男孩一样参加高强度的体育活动，但这在很大程度上是因为成年人相信，这样能让她们的身体更强健，便于日后生育。

lines.en: Fortunately, this wasn’t the only reason ancient adults encouraged kids to play.
lines.zh: 好在，这并不是古代大人鼓励孩子玩耍的唯一理由。

lines.en: Athenian philosopher Plato observed that toys like building blocks and miniature farming implements were useful tools for learning the skills needed in adulthood.
lines.zh: 雅典的哲学家柏拉图就注意到，像积木和迷你农具这样的玩具，是学习成年后所需技能的有用工具。

lines.en: That said, many ancient cultures expected children to give up their games and toys as they grew up.
lines.zh: 不过话说回来，许多古代文化都指望孩子长大之后就把游戏和玩具放下。

lines.en: A common Roman phrase described a child “giving up nuts” when taking up their adult responsibilities since nuts were used in a variety of simple games.
lines.zh: 罗马有一句常用语，用「放下坚果」来形容一个人开始承担成人的责任——因为坚果是很多简单游戏里常用的道具。

lines.en: And young Roman girls left their dolls as offerings to the gods as part of preparing for their wedding.
lines.zh: 而罗马的少女则会把自己的娃娃献给神灵，作为准备出嫁的一部分。

lines.en: However, other childhood games resembled those men and women continued to enjoy into adulthood.
lines.zh: 不过也有一些童年游戏，跟人们成年之后依然爱玩的东西很像。

lines.en: One, called knucklebones, was popular across the ancient Mediterranean.
lines.zh: 其中一种叫「踝骨游戏」，在整个古代地中海地区都很流行。

lines.en: Usually crafted from the ankle bones of sheep or pigs, they could be used as jacks or dice, with different faces earning different point values.
lines.zh: 它通常是用羊或猪的踝骨做成的，既可以当抓子儿玩，也能当骰子用，不同的面朝上算不同的点数。

lines.en: In addition to games of chance, ancient adults played a variety of strategic board games, which may have been introduced during childhood.
lines.zh: 除了碰运气的游戏，古代的大人还玩各种讲策略的棋盘游戏，而这些很可能是他们童年时就接触到的。

lines.en: Some particularly well-recorded examples include the Royal Game of Ur in ancient Mesopotamia, Go in China, Senet in Egypt, and Ludus latrunculorum— or, the Game of Soldiers— in Rome.
lines.zh: 其中记载比较清楚的有：古代美索不达米亚的乌尔王室游戏、中国的围棋、埃及的塞尼特棋，以及罗马的 Ludus latrunculorum，也就是「士兵棋」。

lines.en: Today, playful kids follow the same instincts as their ancient ancestors.
lines.zh: 今天，爱玩的孩子依然遵循着和远古祖先一样的本能。

lines.en: They continue to make up ball games, invent stories for their favorite dolls, and send toy cars skittering across the floor.
lines.zh: 他们照样自己发明球类游戏，给心爱的娃娃编故事，让玩具车在地板上飞快地滑过。

lines.en: Because the simplest kinds of play never get old.
lines.zh: 因为最简单的那种玩耍，永远不会过时。
